summary: Columbus City Schools urges the FCC to preserve E‑Rate support for core infrastructure, maintain a broad definition of educational purposes, avoid federal screen‑time limits, keep device‑ownership distinctions, and strengthen CIPA while allowing state/local flexibility. Columbus City Schools argues that broadband connectivity alone does not guarantee affordability or reliability, and therefore E‑Rate support should not be narrowed or eliminated. Columbus City Schools urges the FCC to maintain and refine E‑Rate support, emphasizing affordability, equity, and a broad definition of educational use. Columbus City Schools argues against imposing uniform screen‑time limits or detailed student‑level reporting on E‑Rate funding, while supporting the current educational‑purpose standard and a reasonableness‑based CIPA framework. Columbus City Schools argues for a narrower scope of CIPA responsibility, technology‑neutral standards, and cautions against reducing E‑Rate participation due to safety impacts. Columbus City Schools argues against federal screen‑time limits in E‑Rate, supports state/local instructional autonomy, and calls for streamlined procurement rules that respect existing state and local laws.
